method_matrix.review: Actual PosM ownership, positive spends, exact caller spend/refund and all native/ERC20/WETH prefunds are checked. Native funds use msg.value rather than pulling WETH. The unused-wrapper approval assertion is deliberately retired; active token/Permit2 allowance and expiration cleanup remain.
Same LP NFT grows without minting another; exact caller ETH/token deltas are added. Only unused native-wrapper approval coupling retires.

Native receipts are ETH, not freshly minted WETH. Actual Core donation fee growth can round, so the actual-Core case bounds receipts and checks a second collection is empty; the unchanged deterministic foundation case retains exact +17 ETH/+29 token cash accounting and prefund assertions.

Actual principal amounts return in ETH and the pool token, with exact physical deltas and destroyed PosM ownership. Requiring no native ETH at the Vault contradicts current native custody and raw ETH/ZZZ exit.

Real Core dirty sync is reset; exact native input and token output deltas and no Manager residual are checked. The fabricated 0.99 output is replaced by output below gross input and above the requested floor.
Real native output goes directly to the caller and retains forced Manager ETH; token input is exact. Fixed fake 0.99/WETH output is not a current guarantee.

The 1000 ETH/980 ETH replacement proves rollback but its minimum-output check masks removal of the exact-input check. The unchanged foundation short-fill-by-one case still covers that guard. A new actual-Core narrow-range observation proves a partial fill whose output meets the oracle floor, followed by an exact Slippage rejection and full state equality; its execution is recorded separately.

Actual LP/protocol fees and price impact cause the deliberately excessive minimum to reject. Price and caller cash remain unchanged. An additional Manager-zero assertion in this exact test is not retained, but other native cases assert the Manager balance and the revert restores its initial zero balance.
Unsolicited native transfer and unauthenticated callback both reject.

Registry native identity, not a WETH accounting substitute, controls native entry. Current negative admission preserves ETH/token funds and next PosM ID. Native and WETH feeds/admission are separately tested; an unused wrapper cannot disable custody.

Both old and first replacement sent zero msg.value and accepted any revert, so a later value check could hide removal of the uint128 bound. The repaired method supplies matching native value for oversized amount0 and amount1, poisons later pool reads, requires exact InvalidAmount, and checks cash/position/allowances unchanged. Production already had the early guard.
Hooked native keys reject and do not mint a PosM NFT. This remains a hookless-only deployment; no hook implementation is added.
The dynamic-fee key rejects and does not mint a PosM NFT. The two old methods are merged; their policy checks both remain.

Current native mint/increase do not unwrap WETH, so a broken unused withdraw must not block them. Exact native cash/refunds and unspent token/prefund/allowance safety replace the obsolete failure requirement.

Native collection does not deposit into WETH. Its fee liability must survive actual delivery failure, now tested with a rejecting ETH recipient and successful later retry rather than an irrelevant wrapper deposit failure.

The unchanged foundation retainNative fault preserves user ETH/token balances and next ID. Actual PosM fee-netting supplies a second real residual case: increase before harvest rejects, then harvest/increase succeeds. An intentionally broken PosM is not presented as real venue behavior.

Foundation still injects forced ETH from the expected Core take path and checks caller balances. The actual-Core case separately forces ETH back during recipient forwarding, verifies failure/Manager zero and permits a clean retry. These are distinct injection points, not identical tests.
